variables.name: Soil moisture
variables.description: Monthly soil moisture from one dataset at a time: GLDAS-2.1 Noah 0–10 cm model layer, or SMAP L3 Enhanced (≈0–5 cm satellite retrieval), version 005 or 006.
variables.annual_value: equal-weight mean of 12 usable monthly means
variables.spatial_resolution: 0.25° GLDAS grid; SMAP enhanced 9 km product sampled on the EE geographic grid (not sensing resolution)
variables.region_unsupported_reason: Soil moisture uses the native grid cell containing the point; region-wide analysis is not implemented.

availability.provisional: Recent observations may be incomplete or provisional; eligibility is evaluated after retrieval.

geographic_limitations: GLDAS: modelled land, 60°S–90°N; Greenland screening and water/ice masks apply.
SMAP: approximately 85°S–85°N; swath and retrieval-quality masks apply.

products.title: GLDAS-2.1 Noah land surface model, 0-10 cm soil moisture (3-hourly, 0.25 degree)
products.citation: Beaudoing, H. and M. Rodell, NASA/GSFC/HSL (2020), GLDAS Noah Land Surface Model L4 3 hourly 0.25 x 0.25 degree V2.1, Greenbelt, Maryland, USA, Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC). https://doi.org/10.5067/E7TYRXPJKWOQ
limitations: Land surface model output driven by meteorological forcing; not an observation.
Layer water storage in kg m-2 (1 kg m-2 = 1 mm of water in the 0-10 cm layer).
The derived m3 m-3 value (storage / 100) is a 0-10 cm model layer mean. It is not equivalent to SMAP's approximately 0-5 cm satellite retrieval.
Forcing changes can create artificial trends: an unexplained shift in AGRMET climatology after 2011, and a radiation-forcing switch to GALWEM on 2025-06-09.
Recent months may be Early-stream products without GPCP precipitation that are later superseded; they are provisional and excluded from trend inference.
Whether soil moisture includes frozen water is not stated in the product documentation (unverified).
Coverage is 60S-90N over modelled land; ocean, inland water, Antarctica, and ice sheets are not supported.
Errors are largest where forcing is uncertain: high latitudes, high altitudes, and regions with sparse rain gauges.

availability.provisional: GLDAS provisional months are excluded from inference.

products.title: SMAP Enhanced L3 Radiometer Global and Polar Grid Daily 9 km EASE-Grid Soil Moisture, Version 5 (AM overpass)
products.native_grid: EE geographic 0.08 degree sampling grid; enhanced 9 km product grid, not effective sensing resolution
products.temporal_sampling: daily overpass (06:00 local solar time, descending), when retrieved
products.citation: O'Neill, P. E., Chan, S., Njoku, E. G., Jackson, T., Bindlish, R., Chaubell, J. & Colliander, A. (2021). SMAP Enhanced L3 Radiometer Global and Polar Grid Daily 9 km EASE-Grid Soil Moisture. (SPL3SMP_E, Version 5). Boulder, Colorado USA. NASA National Snow and Ice Data Center Distributed Active Archive Center. https://doi.org/10.5067/4DQ54OUIJ9DL
limitations: Satellite retrieval from L-band brightness temperature; values are retrieved volumetric content of roughly the top 5 cm, an approximate sensing depth rather than a sharp layer boundary.
Not equivalent to GLDAS 0-10 cm soil moisture, including GLDAS values converted to m3 m-3: depth, footprint (9 km vs 0.25 degree), and method (retrieval vs model) all differ.

Missing data are non-random: no retrieval outside the daily swath, and retrievals are skipped or fail quality control over frozen ground, open water, dense vegetation, urban areas, and radio-frequency interference.
Monthly values are means of valid sampled days, not true monthly means.
The enhanced 9 km product spacing is not the effective radiometer sensing resolution; the displayed polygon represents the Earth Engine sampling cell, not an antenna footprint.
AM (06:00 descending) overpass only; AM and PM are never averaged.
Mission accuracy requirement is 0.04 m3 m-3, which can be comparable to multi-year changes.
Version 005 only. Months after this collection ends are never filled from version 006, and the two versions are never concatenated or averaged.
Version 005 is retired at NSIDC; the record ends in December 2023.

availability.provisional: Quality-filtered sampled days; missing observations remain missing.

caveats: Mann-Kendall significance is reported only after a lag-1 serial-dependence screen. An independent Monte Carlo check (5,000 replications) found that this screened test can reject a true no-trend hypothesis more often than the nominal 5% when annual values are autocorrelated (about 10.5% at n = 45, lag-1 autocorrelation 0.3). Treat 'statistically significant' as indicative, not as a guaranteed 5% false-positive rate.
